title: Walkthrough of setting up Pixel Lab for sweet 2D pixel animations
author: Comet7777
selftext:
I kept fighting AI-generated sprite sheets that came out super janky with 4-6 frames. For a new mech JRPG idea I tried an experiment: same characters, one animated from Lovable (Gemini image gen) sprites with code, one sent to Pixel Lab. The end result is Pixel Lab led to significantly smoother animations upon a single prompt. (ps - zero affiliation with Pixel Lab.)

Here’s what worked for me:

* Try the trial, I did to test it out for my own use case. You get 40 free generations. Use them on your worst animations to see if it’s worth it before paying ($12/mo for 2,000).
* Pixel Lab’s “Vibe Coding” page gives you the MCP config with your token already in it. Paste it into Claude’s config file.
* Give Claude rules up front, or it’ll burn your generations. For example: we write art gen prompts together first, I make stills in free tools (Lovable/Gemini), we try animating in code, and Claude only calls Pixel Lab if code can’t make it smoothly.
* Consistency matters. If your heroes animates smoothly and your enemies don’t, players notice. Go all in or pick a deliberately choppier style. We have to fight the AI slop label lol

Full walkthrough if you want it: [https://youtu.be/NUPr7XNtNS4](https://youtu.be/NUPr7XNtNS4)

comments.author: Dakroh_88
comments.body: Could try my method and my tools i built for something like this. Basic idea is you only need a single image of your character or whatever. Generate a 3d model then have claude rig and animate that 3d model in blender then bring it back to my site and reupload the animation files then render all viewports/angles (2d) out for whatever type of game you are making. Can select pixels at which you want it to be in.  Everything i offer is client side in your browser. The 3d part requires a [fal.ai](http://fal.ai) api key,  which a  model can cost you from $0.10 to $1.50 depending on selected model. Rest is basically your claude subscription. Check it out [https://www.keyframe.it.com/](https://www.keyframe.it.com/)

comments.author: EtadanikM
comments.body:
Yeah, so Pixel Lab is a great example of the sort of service that you can't just vibe code its replacement, because it's not just software - it's a bunch of proprietary fine-tuned generative models running on their serving infra. 

To replicate it, you'd have to fine-tune your own models on expensive GPUs, and then serve them on expensive GPUs. Not something the average person will be able to do. So a service like this will continue to offer value until such a time as the frontier labs are offering the same service through their own models/subscriptions.

It's the same reason Tripo, Eleven Labs, etc. have taken off lately - to make up for the deficiencies frontier labs leave.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body: Yup. I’ve tried to brute force my way to a solution and it’s very painful. Having trained models to solve a narrow problem is my favorite use case for AI.
